name: External Deterrence Failure and Intervention Risk
title: US–China · External deterrence failure and intervention risk

definition.question: How eroded is US and allied deterrence over Taiwan and how close are external powers to direct military intervention?
definition.low_end: Strong, credible and unambiguous US and allied deterrence with regular coordinated presence and no imminent need for direct intervention.
definition.high_end: Deterrence has collapsed and the US and allies are engaged in direct combat operations to defend Taiwan against a PLA attack.

readings.rationale: No graded claims available to assess. Would be higher with evidence of US/allied signals of abandonment, reduced arms sales or presence, or conversely imminent intervention deployments; lower with evidence of strengthened security commitments, pre-positioned stockpiles, and allied operational coordination. Research needed on US policy statements, arms transfers, force posture in Indo-Pacific, and…
